from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Bridge: The Concept of Limits", [
            "Limits allow us to approach points precisely.",
            "Zooming in reveals the curve's local slope.",
            "Straight lines approximate curves at microscopic scales."
        ])
        
        # Setup plot elements
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-1, 3, 1], y_range=[-1, 3, 1], axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: x**2, color=WHITE)
        point = Dot(axes.c2p(1, 1), color=YELLOW)
        
        # Using placeholder for the "zooming" visual
        area = self.place_in_area(VGroup(axes, curve, point), 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.add(area)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Limits allow us to approach points precisely.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00CED1"))
        
        # Animate approach
        h = ValueTracker(1.0)
        line = always_redraw(lambda: axes.get_secant_slope_group(
            x=1, graph=curve, dx=h.get_value(), secant_line_color=YELLOW, 
            secant_line_length=4, dx_label="dx", dy_label="dy"
        ))
        self.add(line)
        self.play(h.animate.set_value(0.1), run_time=2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Zooming in reveals the curve's local slope.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00CED1"))
        self.play(area.animate.scale(2).move_to(self.grid['C3']), run_time=2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Straight lines approximate curves at microscopic scales.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00CED1"))
        
        val_label = Text("Limit: slope -> 2", color=WHITE, font_size=20)
        self.place_at_grid(val_label, 'F5')
        self.play(Write(val_label))
        
        self.play(h.animate.set_value(0.01), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Derivatives measure the rate of change precisely.",
            "The speedometer shows instantaneous speed changes.",
            "The derivative represents the curve's slope."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Differentiation: Measuring Change", lecture_lines)
        
        # --- Animation components ---
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 4, 1], y_range=[0, 4, 1], axis_config={"include_tip": False}, x_length=4, y_length=4)
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.25 * x**3, color="#FF4500")
        
        # Place axes area
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B2", "E5", scale_factor=0.8)
        curve.match_y(axes)
        curve.match_x(axes)
        
        # Speedometer asset
        speedometer = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/speedometer.svg")
        self.place_at_grid(speedometer, "A5", scale_factor=0.3)
        
        point = ValueTracker(1.0)
        
        # Tangent line (simplified to avoid complex redraw)
        tangent = Line(start=LEFT*0.5, end=RIGHT*0.5, color="#FFFF00")
        
        # Setup slope label
        slope_text = Text("Slope: ", font_size=20, color="#FFFFFF")
        slope_val = DecimalNumber(0.75, num_decimal_places=2, font_size=20, color="#FFFFFF")
        slope_group = VGroup(slope_text, slope_val).arrange(RIGHT)
        self.place_at_grid(slope_group, "F2", scale_factor=1.0)

        # Udpater for tangent and value
        def update_tangent(t):
            x = point.get_value()
            y = 0.25 * x**3
            t.move_to(axes.c2p(x, y))
            t.set_angle(np.arctan(0.75 * x**2))
            
        def update_val(v):
            v.set_value(0.75 * point.get_value()**2)
            
        tangent.add_updater(update_tangent)
        slope_val.add_updater(update_val)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF4500"))
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(curve))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        self.play(FadeIn(speedometer))
        self.add(tangent)
        self.play(point.animate.set_value(3.0), run_time=3)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.play(FadeIn(slope_group))
        self.play(point.animate.set_value(1.0), run_time=2)
        
        # Remove updaters before end
        self.wait(1)
        tangent.remove_updater(update_tangent)
        slope_val.remove_updater(update_val)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Integration reverses the process of differentiation.", "We sum infinite tiny rectangles for area.", "Total distance is the accumulation of speed."]
        self.setup_layout("Integration: Accumulating the Whole", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define Curve
        func = lambda x: 0.5 * np.sin(2 * x) + 1
        curve = FunctionGraph(func, x_range=[-1.5, 1.5], color=GREEN)
        self.place_in_area(curve, 'A1', 'D6', scale_factor=0.7)
        
        # Rectangles holder
        rects = VGroup()

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Create(curve), self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(BLUE)
        
        # Build rectangles iteratively to show "summing infinite tiny rectangles"
        for i in range(1, 11):
            n = 2**i
            new_rects = VGroup(*[
                Rectangle(height=func(x), width=3.0/n, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.3)
                for x in np.linspace(-1.5 + 1.5/n, 1.5 - 1.5/n, n)
            ])
            new_rects.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0).move_to(curve.get_bottom() + [0, 1.5, 0])
            self.play(ReplacementTransform(rects, new_rects), run_time=0.3)
            rects = new_rects
        
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        area_label = Text("Total Area", font_size=24, color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(area_label, 'E3')
        
        self.play(Flash(rects, color=YELLOW), Write(area_label))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Fundamental Connection", [
            "Differentiation and integration are inverse operations.",
            "We slice motion and glue it back together.",
            "The fundamental theorem links these two ideas."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        deriv_op = MathTex(r"\frac{d}{dx}", color="#FFD700").scale(1.5)
        int_op = MathTex(r"\int dx", color="#FFD700").scale(1.5)
        equals = MathTex(r"=", color="#FFFFFF").scale(2.0)
        
        self.place_at_grid(deriv_op, 'B2')
        self.place_at_grid(int_op, 'B5')
        self.place_at_grid(equals, 'C3')
        
        # Animation
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        self.play(FadeIn(deriv_op), FadeIn(int_op))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        self.play(Rotate(deriv_op, angle=PI/4), Rotate(int_op, angle=-PI/4))
        self.play(Rotate(deriv_op, angle=-PI/4), Rotate(int_op, angle=PI/4))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        self.play(FadeIn(equals))
        self.play(Flash(equals, color="#FFFFFF", line_length=0.2))

outline.topic: The Essence of Calculus: From Motion to Infinity
outline.target_audience: High school students or curious beginners

sections.title: The Problem: How Fast is the Cheetah Moving?
sections.content: Introduce the limitation of average speed. Calculus begins when we try to find the instantaneous speed of an object (like a sprinting cheetah) at an exact point in time, where distance and time change become 'almost' zero.
sections.example: A cheetah runs 100 meters in 5 seconds. Average speed is easy (20 m/s), but how fast is it running at exactly the 2-second mark?

sections.title: The Bridge: The Concept of Limits
sections.content: Explain 'Limits' as the prerequisite. We zoom into a graph, getting closer and closer to a point without ever needing to land exactly on it. This visual 'zooming in' allows us to define the tangent slope.
sections.example: Animation: A line on a graph getting closer to a curve until the straight line and the curve appear identical at a microscopic level.

sections.title: Differentiation: Measuring Change
sections.content: Define the derivative as the 'slope of the curve.' If the y-axis is distance and the x-axis is time, the derivative is the speedometer of the cheetah. It tells us how the function is changing at any single instant.
sections.example: Visual: A speedometer needle on the cheetah's dashboard that changes value fluidly as the cheetah accelerates.

sections.title: Integration: Accumulating the Whole
sections.content: Introduce Integration as the reverse process. If we know the speed at every moment, how do we find the total distance covered? We break the area under a curve into infinite tiny rectangles and sum them up.
sections.example: Visual: A complex, wavy shape on a screen being filled by an infinite number of razor-thin vertical bars that perfectly sum up to the total area.

sections.title: The Fundamental Connection
sections.content: Conclude by showing that Differentiation (slicing into pieces) and Integration (gluing pieces together) are inverse operations—the 'Fundamental Theorem of Calculus'.
sections.example: The cheetah analogy: Differentiation turns 'total distance' into 'instant speed'; Integration turns 'instant speed' back into 'total distance'.
